endorsements.quote: When such laws apply to a research project, researchers are required by law to grant access to certain types of data upon request, and researchers, IRBs, or others cannot block or override such access
Thus, a first step in developing a protocol on IRRs is to contact the responsible personnel at one’s institution to assess which laws apply to the research.
We encourage approaches that include research participants in the evaluation of potential benefits and potential risks ( Wilkins et al. 2019 ).

unlisted_practices: Use a defined, common terminology to inform researcher decision-making and IRB review of return of individual research results policies.
Decide on returning individual research results on a study-by-study basis and document the choices made.
Assess each data stream's potential benefit and risk of harm as high, low, or unknown and apply presumptive default rules to decide whether to return it.
Communicate IRB-approved decisions on return of results to participants as part of obtaining informed consent.
Review and revise the return of individual research results approach at least annually.
Predefine return thresholds and protocols and communicate them to all stakeholders when results are returned in real time.
Prepare point-of-data-delivery disclosures accompanying returned data, covering data-quality uncertainties, warnings against misuse, and privacy protection.
Explain the limits of validity and potential for bias to participants when returning results generated by AI/ML systems with unknown training data representativeness.
Exercise more caution in returning data and results processed solely by machine learning without a human in the loop.
Estimate the resources required to return promised results and build them into the study design and funding request.
Give participants options about which data to receive and when to receive it.
Consider participants' cultural background, values, and lived experience when deciding how to return results.
Include risks and benefits to third parties in the risk/benefit assessment of returning results.
Choose privacy-protective methods of returning results so that only the participant receives the information.
Avoid excessive alerts to prevent alarm fatigue in participants.

screen.reason: Expert working group framework providing guidelines for ethical return of individual research results from digital phenotyping and AI in psychiatry.
